title: Advanced agents: subagents, A2A, orchestration and tracking

questions.q: What comes back to the main agent when a subagent finishes?
options: Nothing: the subagent answers the user directly
Only the subagent's final answer, as the Task tool result
questions.why: The subagent's context stays with the subagent.

questions.q: How does the main agent decide which subagent to call?
options: From the description in the subagent's Markdown header
questions.why: Write a specific description: it's the only thing the main agent sees.

questions.q: A subagent file has no tools line. What can that subagent use?
options: Every built-in tool, including Bash and Write
Only the tools of the main agent
questions.why: Always list the tools: least privilege.

questions.q: In the lab, the main agent's prompt grew from about 1,700 to about 2,000 tokens. What did it receive?
questions.why: The raw files stayed in the subagent's context (up to ~2,200 tokens).

questions.q: What is a real cost of subagents, seen in the lab?
options: More model calls and more total tokens, so slower answers
questions.why: 5 calls instead of 3, about 1.5 minutes instead of about half a minute.

questions.q: What does A2A connect?
options: An agent to another agent, which has its own model and tools
questions.why: MCP connects an agent to tools; A2A to other agents.

questions.q: Where does an A2A agent publish its agent card?
questions.why: Clients read it to discover the agent's skills and URL.

questions.q: In the response to SendMessage, where is the remote agent's answer?
questions.why: A message becomes a task; the result comes back as artifacts.

questions.q: Why did the lab set a2a.authorization.required=false?
options: The SDK refuses every task without an authorization provider: OK only for a local lab
questions.why: Keep authorization on for any server others can reach.

questions.q: The inventory agent said 'restock on 2026-12-03'. The sales agent said 'not before Christmas'. What does it show?
options: The protocol moved the right fact; the final agent reasoned wrongly
questions.why: Compute dates and numbers in code, or return structured data.

questions.q: What is the 'best of both' way to orchestrate agents?
options: The model plans; Java executes the plan, checks it and enforces the rules
questions.why: Model-driven planning, code-driven execution.

questions.q: Why do the agents exchange Java records (Plan, Finding, Review)?
options: So the code can check and decide with real types instead of free text
questions.why: Structured output between agents.

questions.q: In the first run, why was the root cause wrong?
options: The planner forgot the deploys worker, so nobody looked at the deployment
questions.why: A team is only as good as its plan.

questions.q: How did the lab fix it?
options: A runbook rule in Java: always add a deploys step
questions.why: Put non-negotiable rules in code.

questions.q: The budget was 1,500 tokens but the team used 2,556. Why?
options: The workers were already running in parallel when the budget ran out
questions.why: A check before each call can't stop calls in flight: keep a margin.

questions.q: What is a span?
options: One step of a request: a name, a duration, a parent and tags
questions.why: A trace is a tree of spans.

questions.q: What does Spring AI trace for you once Actuator and a tracing starter are added?
options: ChatClient calls, advisors, model calls (with gen_ai token tags) and tool executions
questions.why: You add your own spans per agent step on top.

questions.q: In the lab, one request gave four traces. Why?
options: The workers ran on new virtual threads that started without the trace context
Each agent used a different model
questions.why: Wrap the executor with ContextExecutorService.wrap(...).

questions.q: Which tag is fine on the agent.tokens metric?
questions.why: Keep tags low cardinality.

questions.q: The trace showed the deploys worker took 68 s for a tiny tool. Why?
options: One local Ollama served three parallel workers, so calls partly waited in line
questions.why: Traces reveal the real bottleneck.

questions.q: What comes back to the main agent from a subagent?
Why always write a tools line in a subagent file?
options: Without it the subagent gets every built-in tool, even Bash and Write

questions.q: Subagents usually make the total token count...
options: Go up: more model calls, but a smaller main context

questions.q: MCP connects an agent to tools. A2A connects an agent to...
options: Another agent with its own model and tools

questions.q: What does a client read first to use an A2A agent?
In A2A, where is the result of a task?
Which A2A setting must never be turned off on a reachable server?
The best orchestration split is:
options: The model plans; Java executes the plan and enforces the rules

questions.q: A worker times out. A good orchestrator...
options: Records it as a finding and continues

questions.q: A shared token budget checked before each call can still be exceeded because...
options: Parallel calls already in flight finish anyway

questions.q: Parallel workers show up as separate traces. The fix is...
Which is a good tag for per-agent metrics?

challenge.title: A traced travel-planner team
challenge.task: Build a travel planner with a supervisor agent, two local subagents and one remote agent over A2A, and trace it end to end.
requirements: A supervisor that delegates with the Task tool to two subagents (e.g. flights and hotels), each defined in a Markdown file with a tools line
A third agent (e.g. weather) running as a separate A2A server with an agent card
Typed hand-offs: the supervisor returns a Java record with the plan, the costs and the sources
A per-agent token counter and a token budget for the whole team
One trace per request in Zipkin, including the parallel work; check whether it crosses the A2A call
A short note: one thing the trace showed that the logs didn't
selfCheck: The supervisor really delegates: the log shows Task calls to all three agents
One request gives exactly one trace in Zipkin (or you can explain where it breaks)
You can say which agent costs the most tokens, and why
